candidates.counter_evidence_explanation: Peer services show flat memory and low latency, so the leak is isolated to order; retained bytes remain below the 160MB limit and p95 is 73ms, so user impact is not yet proven.
missing_evidence: Order heap growth trend beyond the 5-minute window to confirm unbounded growth
Order p95 latency and error rate over a longer window to link retention to checkout degradation
candidates.statement: Order service shows sustained heap retention: retained bytes rose from 49.4MB to 81.4MB across 5 samples with positive net allocations and no reclamation after GC, plus 11 retained_heap_after_gc warnings. This bounded memory-leak pattern in order is the only evidence-supported root cause for degraded checkout health.
candidates.uncertainty: Retention is below the configured limit and latency is normal; causal link to checkout degradation is not yet established.

report.explanation: Order is the only service with anomalous memory retention (sustained positive net retention after GC, 11 retained_heap_after_gc warnings), while gateway, payment and inventory are healthy. Deployment record alone does not establish causation. Candidate is bounded to the observed memory-leak pattern; impact linkage remains uncertain.
